answer: All 18 Experimental Economics (project == 'ee') original studies in the dataset were conducted in a lab setting — a proportion of 18/18 = 100% (0% online). Lab setting is inferred as non-online (online.o == 0), the only lab/online signal available in the data; it is corroborated by subjects.o (17 'students', 1 'community', none 'online'). The ee subset contains exactly one row per unique O/R pair, so the study-based and row-based proportions are identical (100%).

payload.hypothesis: Hypothesis: In the Experimental Economics replication project (project == 'ee'), essentially all original studies were conducted in a physical lab setting rather than online. The dataset contains 18 unique original studies (one row per O/R pair, ee.1–ee.18), and every one has online.o == 0 (not online), giving a lab-based proportion of 18/18 = 100%. 'Lab' is inferred as non-online because the dataset has no direct lab/online field; the inference is corroborated by subjects.o ('students' for 17 studies, 'community' for 1; none 'online'). This contrasts with psychology projects (rpp/ml1/ml3), where online experiments occur.
payload.workflow: 1) Loaded data/meta-regression_study_data_heterogeneity_in_replication_projects.csv (927 rows, 57 columns, 141 unique O/R pairs). 2) Filtered project == 'ee' → 18 rows / 18 unique ids (verified no multi-lab duplication; lab_id NA for all ee rows). 3) Verified no exclusions: drop == False and aggregated empty for all 18 rows. 4) Deduplicated on id (stated no-op). 5) Computed proportion = mean(online.o == 0) over unique original studies = 18/18 = 1.0 (100%); row-based proportion check also 100%. 6) Reported supporting distributions: online.o {0: 18, 1: 0, NA: 0}; subjects.o {'students': 17, 'community': 1}; us_lab.o treated as lab-country indicator, not used. Script: artifacts/analysis_ee_lab_proportion.py.
